chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abu Muhammad Al-Wabishi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

One of our companions asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who bought his father from the zakat, the zakat of his wealth. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He has bought the best of slaves; there is no problem with that.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Can a person use their zakat money to buy their own father's freedom from slavery?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) validates the use of zakat funds to emancipate a specific individual, even one's own father, highlighting the flexibility of zakat categories for *riqab* (freeing slaves). The description 'the best of slaves' underscores the spiritual merit of prioritizing close kin for liberation, a concept deeply rooted in Shia jurisprudence where freeing a slave is a primary objective of zakat distribution. This ruling illustrates the practical application of zakat not just as wealth purification, but as a tool for social and familial emancipation.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Abu Muhammad Al Wabishy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘One of our companions asked himasws about a man who buys his own father (who was a slave), from the Zakāt, the Zakāt of his wealth’. Heasws said: ‘he has bought the best of slave. There is no problem with it’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from abu Muhammad al-Wabishiy who has said the following: “

Certain persons of our people asked abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who has purchased with money from Zakat of his assets his own father. He (the Imam) said, ‘He has purchased the best slave and it is not harmful.’”
